alternatives_rejected.why: Injected delay raises latency but would not drive a +5867.8% (z=629.73) CPU jump in the same service. Latency z=7219 is consistent with requests queuing behind a saturated CPU (E1, E5).
Memory deviation (z=84.05, +420%) is an order of magnitude weaker than the CPU deviation (z=629.73) (E1). Memory growth is plausibly a side effect of request backlog.

alternatives_rejected.candidate: other services on the slow path (checkoutservice, paymentservice, currencyservice, etc.)
alternatives_rejected.why: The all-services metric ranking shows every top deviation belongs to emailservice (E1). The slow traces all pass through emailservice (E3), but they only show full paths, not per-span latency, so the traces fit an emailservice cause without isolating it. E2 shows only routine INFO lines, all from emailservice.

proposed_fix.description: First, scale out emailservice replicas and raise its CPU limit to relieve checkout latency. Then profile the emailservice pod (e.g., top or py-spy) to find and stop the runaway CPU consumer. Restarting the pod or killing the process is a separate destructive step that needs approval.
